credit_headline.narrative: Bank credit growth is still running hot: non-food credit grew 18.77% YoY in August 2026, and even with a 0.29-point dip from July's 19.06% it remains well above the 15.5% mark that bounds the top quarter of readings in this window. The level sits at or near the maximum of this window, with no pause in the expansion.
sibc-bank-credit-abs.inference: August's ₹3.1L Cr addition is larger than July's ₹1.5L Cr gain, keeping bank credit at a fresh all-time high of ₹223.9L Cr in this 36-period record.

sibc-pl-vehicle-yoy.title: Vehicle loan growth climbs to 19.7% — a fresh high

sibc-pl-yoy-scan.title: Gold loans still lead personal loans at 83.2% YoY growth
sibc-pl-yoy-scan.observation: Loans against gold jewellery grew 83.2% YoY in Aug 2026, the fastest among all nine personal loan categories, followed by Advances against Fixed Deposits at 43.2% and Vehicle Loans at 19.7%.

sibc-psl-acceleration.title: PSL acceleration spread narrows to 10.48 points as Renewable Energy reverses
sibc-psl-acceleration.observation: Social Infrastructure is the fastest-accelerating PSL segment this period at +4.74 points, while Renewable Energy is the slowest at -5.74 points.
sibc-psl-acceleration.direction: Renewable Energy flipped from strengthening to weakening (+11.54 points last period → -5.74 points now), and Social Infrastructure flipped from weakening to strengthening (-21.03 points last period → +4.74 points now); the spread across all 10 segments narrowed to 10.48 points from 32.57 points.
chain: Social Infrastructure accelerated the most this period, up 4.74 points, while Renewable Energy decelerated the most, down 5.74 points.
The gap between the fastest- and slowest-accelerating PSL segments is 10.48 points, down sharply from 32.57 points last period.

sibc-psl-agri-yoy.title: PSL Agriculture holds near peak at 19.44% YoY growth
sibc-psl-agri-yoy.observation: PSL Agriculture credit grew 19.44% year-on-year in Aug 2026, barely changed from 19.40% in Jul 2026.
sibc-psl-agri-yoy.direction: Growth moved just 0.04 points, from 19.40% → 19.44%, holding above 15.2%, the high end of its 24-period range.
chain: PSL Agriculture grew 19.44% year-on-year in Aug 2026, up only 0.04 points from 19.40% in Jul 2026.
That keeps the reading above 15.2%, the high end of the 24-period range, matching the level it held in Jun 2026 (19.9%).
Growth has now sat at 19.9% → 19.4% → 19.4% across Jun, Jul and Aug 2026 without extending higher.
sibc-psl-agri-yoy.inference: This is a third straight period above 19%, but the 0.04-point move confirms Agriculture is holding at this elevated growth level rather than climbing further — the same plateau flagged last period, still unbroken.

sibc-psl-allocation.title: MSE take 39.0% of new PSL credit as Housing falls to 5.4%
sibc-psl-allocation.observation: Micro and Small Enterprises captured 39.0% of new PSL credit deployed over the past 12 months, the largest share of any segment, while Housing's share fell to 5.4%.
sibc-psl-allocation.direction: Housing's share of new PSL deployment fell from 11.3% to 5.4%, Weaker Sections fell from 22.2% to 16.4%, and Micro and Small Enterprises rose from 37.2% to 39.0%.
chain: Micro and Small Enterprises now take 39.0% of new PSL credit, up from 37.2% last period, while Housing's share fell to 5.4% from 11.3%.
Rotation mass stands at 39.00 points, meaning a similar scale of reallocation as last period's 37.11 points.

Weaker Sections' share also fell, from 22.2% to 16.4%, leaving Micro and Small Enterprises (39.0%) and Agriculture (26.9%) as the two largest destinations for new PSL credit, with Housing, Educational Loans, Renewable Energy, Social Infrastructure, Export Credit and Others all at or below 5.4%.
sibc-psl-allocation.inference: New PSL credit is rotating away from Housing and Weaker Sections toward Micro and Small Enterprises and Agriculture — Housing's 5.4% share of new deployment is less than half what it was last period (11.3%), the sharpest drop among the ten segments.

sibc-psl-education-yoy.title: PSL Education loans cool further to 15.91% YoY, down 0.80 points
sibc-psl-education-yoy.observation: PSL Educational Loans grew 15.91% year-on-year in Aug 2026, down from 16.70% in Jul 2026.
sibc-psl-education-yoy.direction: Growth decelerated another 0.80 points, from 16.70% → 15.91%, continuing the pullback from 22.3% in Jun 2026.
chain: PSL Educational Loans grew 15.91% year-on-year in Aug 2026, down 0.80 points from 16.70% in Jul 2026.
This is a second straight deceleration after growth broke its run above 22% in Jul 2026, down from 22.3% in Jun 2026.
At 15.91%, growth now sits near the middle of its 24-period range, well below the 22.5% high end it held for several months through Jun 2026.
sibc-psl-education-yoy.inference: Education lending has now decelerated for two consecutive periods — 22.3% → 16.7% → 15.9% — confirming the plateau break flagged last period rather than a one-off dip.

sibc-psl-export-yoy.title: PSL Export Credit Falls to -9.7% YoY, Recovery Stalls
sibc-psl-export-yoy.observation: PSL Export Credit contracted 9.73% year-on-year in Aug 2026.
sibc-psl-export-yoy.direction: The contraction deepened by 0.90 points, from -8.8% → -9.7%, reversing the two-period improvement that had brought it in from -13.7% in Dec 2025 to -8.8% in Jul 2026.
chain: Export credit fell 9.73% YoY in Aug 2026, worsening from -8.84% in Jul 2026 — a 0.90-point deepening.
This breaks the easing trend seen since Dec 2025 (-13.7%), when the contraction had been narrowing period over period toward -8.8% in Jul 2026.
The reading sits near the middle of the 24-period range (p25=-10.5%, p75=7.1%), so the segment remains in the weaker half of its history rather than at an extreme.
sibc-psl-export-yoy.inference: Last period's moderation in Export Credit has not held — the contraction widened again instead of continuing to narrow, putting the segment back in a declining state after one period of relief.

sibc-psl-housing-yoy.title: PSL Housing Growth Cools to 9.6% YoY, Slide Eases
sibc-psl-housing-yoy.observation: PSL Housing credit grew 9.55% year-on-year in Aug 2026.
sibc-psl-housing-yoy.direction: Growth slowed by 1.06 points, from 10.6% → 9.6%, a far smaller drop than the 10.7-point slide from 21.3% to 10.6% in Jul 2026 or the 17.7-point fall from 39.0% to 21.3% in Jun 2026.
chain: Housing credit grew 9.55% YoY in Aug 2026, down from 10.61% in Jul 2026 — a 1.06-point slowdown.
That is much smaller than the preceding drops: 10.7 points in Jul 2026 (21.3% → 10.6%) and 17.7 points in Jun 2026 (39.0% → 21.3%).
The current reading sits near the middle of the 24-period range (p25=0.7%, p75=35.8%), after spending most of this run near its top.
sibc-psl-housing-yoy.inference: The sharp back-to-back decelerations that pulled Housing down from near 40% growth appear to be flattening out — the Aug 2026 slip of 1.06 points is a fraction of the prior two drops, even though growth is still falling.

sibc-psl-medium-yoy.title: PSL Medium Enterprises Hit 31.0% YoY — Third Straight Record
sibc-psl-medium-yoy.observation: PSL Medium Enterprises credit grew 31.01% year-on-year in Aug 2026.
sibc-psl-medium-yoy.direction: Growth accelerated by 1.81 points, from 29.2% → 31.0%, extending the run from 27.5% in Jun 2026.
chain: Medium Enterprises credit grew 31.01% YoY in Aug 2026, up from 29.20% in Jul 2026 — a 1.81-point acceleration.
This is the third consecutive series high, following 27.5% in Jun 2026 and 29.2% in Jul 2026.
The reading is at or near the maximum of the 24-period range, well above the historical p75 of 21.9%.
sibc-psl-medium-yoy.inference: Medium Enterprises have now posted three straight series-high readings (27.5% → 29.2% → 31.0%), the fastest growth in this dataset, with each period adding further acceleration rather than leveling off.

sibc-psl-momentum.title: Micro & Small Enterprises Add ₹6.51L Cr, Still PSL's Biggest Driver
sibc-psl-momentum.observation: Micro and Small Enterprises added ₹6.51 lakh crore in net credit over the past 12 months, the largest addition among 10 PSL segments.
sibc-psl-momentum.direction: Agriculture and Allied Activities added ₹4.49L Cr and Weaker Sections ₹2.74L Cr, while Export Credit (-₹0.01L Cr) and Others (-₹0.01L Cr) were the only two segments to contract.
chain: Micro and Small Enterprises added ₹6.51L Cr over the trailing 12 months, ahead of Agriculture's ₹4.49L Cr and Weaker Sections' ₹2.74L Cr.
8 of the 10 PSL segments posted net additions; only Export Credit (-₹0.01L Cr) and Others (-₹0.01L Cr) contracted.
The spread between the top and bottom segment is ₹6.53L Cr, from Micro & Small at ₹6.51L Cr to Others at -₹0.01L Cr.
sibc-psl-momentum.inference: Micro & Small Enterprises remain the single largest source of PSL credit growth, adding more on its own than Agriculture or Weaker Sections individually, while Export Credit and Others are the only two segments losing ground.

sibc-psl-msme-fy-acceleration.title: PSL MSME credit up 15.9 points FY25 to FY26
sibc-psl-msme-fy-acceleration.observation: PSL MSME credit grew 13.4% in the year ending Mar 2025 and 29.4% in the year ending Mar 2026, a 15.9-point acceleration.
sibc-psl-msme-fy-acceleration.direction: Full-year growth stepped up from 13.4% to 29.4% between FY25 and FY26.
chain: PSL MSME credit grew 13.4% in FY25 and 29.4% in FY26.
The 15.9-point gap between the two years is this signal's acceleration value.
A full-year step-up of this size shows bank deployment to Micro & Small enterprises moved to a materially higher growth rate across the year, not within it.
sibc-psl-msme-fy-acceleration.inference: This 15.9-point step-up is unchanged since the last evaluation — FY26's 29.4% full-year rate more than doubled FY25's 13.4%, the largest full-year acceleration in this dataset.

sibc-psl-msme-yoy.title: PSL Micro & Small credit growth up to 25.95% YoY
sibc-psl-msme-yoy.observation: PSL Micro & Small enterprises credit grew 25.95% year-on-year in Aug 2026.
sibc-psl-msme-yoy.direction: Growth rose 1.89 points, from 24.06% in Jul 2026 to 25.95% in Aug 2026.
chain: PSL Micro & Small enterprises YoY growth rose to 25.95% in Aug 2026, up from 24.06% the prior period.
At 25.95%, the reading sits above this series' p75 mark of 25.6%, the upper end of its range across 24 periods.
The move follows a run between May 2026 (23.7%) and Jul 2026 (24.1%) where growth had eased from the Mar 2026 peak of 29.4%.
sibc-psl-msme-yoy.inference: Growth had held near 24% for three periods (May to Jul 2026) after easing from March's 29.4% peak; the 1.89-point rise to 25.95% in Aug 2026 breaks that plateau and pushes the reading back above the p75 mark of 25.6%, the upper end of this signal's 24-period range.

sibc-psl-others-yoy.title: PSL Others contraction widens again to -3.35% YoY
sibc-psl-others-yoy.observation: PSL Others credit contracted 3.35% year-on-year in Aug 2026.
sibc-psl-others-yoy.direction: The contraction widened by 2.23 points, from -1.12% in Jul 2026 to -3.35% in Aug 2026.
chain: PSL Others YoY growth fell to -3.35% in Aug 2026 from -1.12% in Jul 2026, a 2.23-point widening of the contraction.

Even after widening, -3.35% stays above this series' p75 of -4.9%, so it remains in the milder half of the historical range despite the month-on-month move.
sibc-psl-others-yoy.inference: The four-period run of easing contraction, from -12.5% in Apr 2026 to -1.12% in Jul 2026, has broken: the gap widened back to -3.35% in Aug 2026, interrupting what had looked like a steady path out of contraction.

sibc-psl-renewable-pos-streak.title: PSL Renewable Energy streak extends to 24 periods
sibc-psl-renewable-pos-streak.observation: PSL Renewable Energy credit has posted positive YoY growth for 24 consecutive periods as of Aug 2026.
sibc-psl-renewable-pos-streak.direction: The streak extended from 23 periods in Jul 2026 to 24 in Aug 2026 — positive every period since the series began.
chain: PSL Renewable Energy's positive YoY streak reached 24 periods in Aug 2026, up from 23 the prior period.
24 periods is the maximum value recorded in this series, meaning the streak has held without interruption since it started.
An unbroken run across the full 24-period series means no month in this dataset has recorded negative YoY growth for this segment.
sibc-psl-renewable-pos-streak.inference: At 24 consecutive periods — the full length of the series — Renewable Energy is the only PSL segment evaluated here with no recorded month of YoY contraction.

sibc-psl-renewable-yoy.title: PSL Renewable Energy growth slows to 26% from 31.7%
sibc-psl-renewable-yoy.observation: PSL Renewable Energy grew 25.96% year-on-year in Aug 2026, down from 31.70% in Jul 2026.
sibc-psl-renewable-yoy.direction: Growth decelerated by 5.74 points, from 31.7% → 26.0%, after rising from 15.6% in Apr 2026 to 31.7% in Jul 2026.
chain: Renewable Energy YoY growth fell to 26.0% in Aug 2026 from 31.7% in Jul 2026, a drop of 5.74 points.
This breaks the run that had taken growth from 15.6% in Apr 2026 up to 31.7% in Jul 2026.
At 26.0%, growth is now in the lower range of this 24-period series, below the 33.5% level it has usually exceeded.
sibc-psl-renewable-yoy.inference: The acceleration that lifted Renewable Energy from 15.6% in Apr 2026 to 31.7% in Jul 2026 has broken, and at 26.0% growth is back in the lower range of this 24-period series — close to the 15.6%-20.2% levels it ran at between Apr and Jun 2026.

sibc-psl-share-of-credit-scan.title: Micro & Small Enterprises top PSL mix at 14.1% share
sibc-psl-share-of-credit-scan.observation: Micro and Small Enterprises hold the largest share of all bank credit among priority-sector segments, at 14.1%, ahead of Agriculture and Allied Activities at 12.3% and Weaker Sections at 9.5%.
sibc-psl-share-of-credit-scan.direction: Across 10 segments, 4 are gaining share and 6 are losing it; the gap between the largest (14.1%) and smallest (0.0%) segment is 14.1 points.
chain: Micro and Small Enterprises take 14.1% of all bank credit, the largest priority-sector segment, with Agriculture and Allied Activities next at 12.3% and Weaker Sections at 9.5%.

Three segments — Weaker Sections, Educational Loans and Others — flipped from strengthening to weakening this period, while Social Infrastructure is the only one to flip the other way, from weakening to strengthening.
sibc-psl-share-of-credit-scan.inference: Micro and Small Enterprises' 14.1% share dwarfs the five smallest segments, which together hold under 1% of all bank credit. The sharper move is in direction, not size: Weaker Sections, Educational Loans and Others all turned from gaining to losing share in the same period, while only Social Infrastructure turned the other way.

sibc-psl-size-scan.title: Priority sector lending crosses ₹100L Cr for the first time
sibc-psl-size-scan.observation: The priority sector loan book stood at ₹100.38L Cr in Aug 2026, up from ₹99.07L Cr in Jul 2026.
sibc-psl-size-scan.direction: Size rose ₹1.32L Cr, from ₹99.07L Cr → ₹100.38L Cr, crossing ₹100L Cr for the first time in this 36-period series and sitting at or near its highest level.
chain: The PSL book reached ₹100.38L Cr in Aug 2026, up ₹1.32L Cr from ₹99.07L Cr in Jul 2026.
This continues a steady climb from ₹65.17L Cr in Sep 2023, the start of this 36-period series, through ₹98.39L Cr in Jun 2026.
At ₹100.38L Cr, the book has crossed the ₹100L Cr mark for the first time and is at or near the maximum of the full 36-period range.
sibc-psl-size-scan.inference: The priority sector book has nearly doubled in size from ₹65.17L Cr in Sep 2023 to ₹100.38L Cr now, and this is the first period it has crossed ₹100L Cr, with the level at or near the maximum of this 36-period range.

sibc-psl-social-infra-yoy.title: PSL Social Infrastructure rebounds to 41.5% YoY growth
sibc-psl-social-infra-yoy.observation: PSL Social Infrastructure grew 41.49% year-on-year in Aug 2026, up from 36.76% in Jul 2026.
sibc-psl-social-infra-yoy.direction: Growth turned back up by 4.74 points, from 36.8% → 41.5%, after two straight periods of slowing from the 70.7% peak in May 2026 (57.8% in Jun, 36.8% in Jul).
chain: Social Infrastructure growth rose to 41.5% in Aug 2026, up 4.74 points from 36.8% in Jul 2026.
This follows two consecutive periods of slowing from the 70.7% peak in May 2026, down to 57.8% in Jun and 36.8% in Jul.
At 41.5%, growth is back above the 40.3% level, placing it among the strongest readings in this 24-period series.
sibc-psl-social-infra-yoy.inference: After slowing for two straight periods from the 70.7% peak in May 2026 down to 36.8% in Jul, Social Infrastructure growth has turned back up to 41.5% — back above the 40.3% mark and among the strongest readings in this 24-period series.

sibc-psl-weaker-sections-yoy.title: PSL Weaker Sections growth cools to 14.7%, still above range
sibc-psl-weaker-sections-yoy.observation: PSL Weaker Sections (including PSLC SF/MF) grew 14.73% year-on-year in Aug 2026, down from 15.18% in Jul 2026.
sibc-psl-weaker-sections-yoy.direction: Growth eased 0.45 points, from 15.2% → 14.7%, the second straight monthly slip after peaking at 15.3% in Jun 2026 — but it still sits above the p75 level of 14.4%.
chain: Weaker Sections (incl. PSLC SF/MF) grew 14.73% YoY in Aug 2026, down from 15.18% in Jul 2026 and 15.3% in Jun 2026.
At 14.7%, the reading still sits above the p75 level of 14.4% across 24 periods, keeping it in the upper range even after the slip.
This is the second consecutive monthly decline from the Jun 2026 high of 15.3%, pulling growth off its recent peak.
sibc-psl-weaker-sections-yoy.inference: Weaker Sections growth has eased for two straight periods from the 15.3% high in Jun 2026 to 14.73% now, though it remains above the p75 threshold of 14.4% and well above the May 2026 trough of 9.1%.

sibc-psl-weaker-yoy.title: PSL Weaker Sections YoY growth slips to 14.7% from 15.2%
sibc-psl-weaker-yoy.observation: PSL Weaker Sections grew 14.73% year-on-year in Aug 2026, down from 15.18% in Jul 2026.
sibc-psl-weaker-yoy.direction: Growth fell 0.45 points, from 15.2% → 14.7%, the second straight period of cooling since the 15.3% reading in Jun 2026 — still above the p75 level of 14.4%.
chain: Weaker Sections YoY growth was 14.73% in Aug 2026, down from 15.18% in Jul 2026 and 15.3% in Jun 2026.
